# Kino montage recipe

Photographs, film and documents pressed into one ink-and-paper poster with a single red, cut to a machine beat. Diagonal bands at -18 degrees carry the type. Windows cut on the same axis hold the pictures. Numbers count up, documents get marked in red, and a red circle opens onto the next shot.

## Principles

1. Recut evidence. Use real material only: photographs, footage, scans. The argument lives in the cutting and arrangement, never in illustration.
2. One printed sheet. Every picture goes through the same two-tone print (ink to paper). Red is the sole colour, overprinted as a printed element.
3. The beat edits. Cuts, slams, wipes and counts follow a 120 BPM grid: beat 0.5 s, bar 2 s, hits on a beat, a half-beat or a sixteenth (0.125 s).
4. Type is structure. Words and numbers act as beams: set on a band, as solid blocks, or stacked top to bottom. No floating captions.
5. Crowd over person. Many small figures, hands, machines. No single face as hero.

Not a stage talk or slide deck (no centred headline with bullets, header bars, fades). Not Swiss white space: stay asymmetric and diagonal, with no thin decorative rules. Not a museum slideshow: never show a picture neutrally; window it, stack it, count it.

## Building blocks

- Bands run along the axis, in red or ink.
- Windows hold the pictures: rectangles or parallelograms trimmed to a band's edge.
- Cut-outs: people scissored from photographs, 7 px paper border.
- Type blocks.
- Over everything: one paper-fibre speckle layer, opacity about 0.5.
- Source tab on every picture window (`FOTO · ARSIP DUSUN 2026`). A stand-in must say what it truly is.

## Print grade

A single function for every picture: take luminance, apply the S-curve `x + 0.32·(x−0.5)·(1−|2x−1|)·2`, add a little grain, then `rgb = ink + (paper − ink)·g`. Pictures keep no other colour.

Paint stand-in photos once at load (Canvas 2D, seeded PRNG), grade them, and convert them to images. The user's photos and footage from `list_media` replace stand-ins and take the same grade.

Documents (maps, pages) stay documents: halftone-dot blocks, wavy-line water, dashed roads, labels in letter-spaced capitals. Mark them, do not retype them as slides: a red circle on the place, a red bar across the sentence.

## Palette

- Red: `--utama` (default `#d52b1e`). For bands, wedges, unit blocks, circles, lower thirds, and the restamped key number.
- Paper: `--latar` (`#ede4d0`). Ground, reversed type, light end of the grade.
- Ink: `--teks` (`#141210`), aliased `--tinta`. Type, thin rules, dark grounds, dark end of the grade.
- Text on red: `--teks-di-utama`. Red words on paper: `--utama-di-latar`. On ink grounds, red shows up only as blocks carrying their own text, never as red letters.
- Reversed type is `--kertas` on `--tinta`, both derived from `--latar` and `--teks`, so contrast survives any brand. The grade takes the darker of the two as its ink.
- Do not lay red over red: a red block landing on a red ground flips to ink. Alternate grounds (paper, ink, paper) so cuts register.

## Type

- `--font-judul`: Oswald 700, uppercase. Numbers 360-400 px. Unit blocks 96-130 px. Band text 54-66 px, letter-spacing 0.05em. Lower-third bars 54 px. Stacked vertical letters 150 px on a 150 px pitch.
- `--font-isi`: Space Grotesk 700, uppercase. Tags 20-26 px with letter-spacing 0.1-0.16em. Subtitle strips 28-34 px on an ink bar with a 14 px red tick.
- Set type along the -18 degree axis on a band, or in an ink or red block. Keep it off the frame's centre and out of header position. A number can outsize the words explaining it. Allow slack; a brand font may run wider.

## Timing

- Grid: all events land on multiples of 0.5, 0.25 or 0.125 s. Pictures run 0.5-2 s per shot; hold longer only for reading. To accelerate a section, halve the interval: 0.5, then 0.25, then 0.125 s, with 3 frames as the floor.
- Slam: the element enters from off-frame along the axis in 0.1-0.2 s, `power4.out`, stops dead, then the frame shakes 10-18 px, decaying over 0.28 s.
- Digits stamp one per eighth (0.125 s). A stacked word slams one letter per sixteenth.
- Red wipe: a 260 px red band, perpendicular to the axis (72 degrees), crosses the frame in 0.3 s `power1.inOut`, showing the next scene behind its trailing edge. Land it on a downbeat.
- Iris: a red circle drawn over 0.5 s, then it grows to 1,700 px radius in 0.55 s, `power2.in`, as an aperture onto the next shot.
- Flash cut: one frame at 80% paper on a freeze, followed by a jump-in crop at 1.2x.
- No hold sits still longer than a second. Push a window 1.16x to 1.0x over 3.6 s, climb a counter, or zoom a map 1.0 to 1.7 over 3.2 s while its rotation settles from -3 degrees to 0.
- Ending: half a bar of ink silence with one red dot, then the heaviest hit. Everything locks by about 12.8 s and holds 2 s.

## Camera

- Slam along the axis: weight, a fact landing. Titles, numbers, lower thirds.
- Slow push inside a window: attention without a cut. Hooks, holds.
- Map zoom around a fixed point: locating the story. Places, routes, org charts.
- Iris from a circle: from "where" to "what happened there". Place to scene.
- Red wipe: a new section. Chapter changes.
- Tilt up a tall window: growth, completion. Results.
- Flash and jump-in: stress the object. Proof, close-ups.

## Signature moves

- Title package: a red band slams on the axis, a window cut to its top edge plays a photo, digits stamp, the unit sits on a red block. For a community project's days, a shop anniversary, a channel's season opener, a class syllabus.
- Map plus iris: a tilted document map pushes in; a red circle drawn on the place then opens onto the scene. For an event location, a delivery area, a field trip, a story's setting.
- Vertical title: letters stacked top to bottom beside a tall slanted window, a date on a band across the picture, a counter climbing inside a red tab. For a volunteer drive's headcount, workshop attendees, subscribers gained, a team's steps.
- Silence, then the heaviest hit: ink frame, one red dot, then huge numbers slam beside the finished subject. For a result reveal, an opening day, a milestone, a final score.
- Document marked, not quoted: a red bar over the exact sentence, the number repeated huge in a block. For a price list, a rule, a receipt, a quote from a letter.

## Avoid

- Upscaled photos go to mush. Window them and keep zooms modest.
- Type drifting off a band. Position it from the band's centre line, not by eye.
- Red on red. Ink type over a dark photo edge (add a tab or keep the edge clear).
- A face as hero. A document with three highlights (mark one sentence per shot). Labels inside a 1/8-beat cut, which is too quick to read; put text in the holds.
- Counters that read as fact: halt the count on whatever value a caption states.
- A stand-in painted photo passed off as real. Tag it honestly.
- Slow load painting: stay near one second with few, small canvases and one grain tile, and convert each to an image once.

# Constructivist montage: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 0.5, medium 1.0, long 2.0.

## hook

- en: a red band slams along the -18 degree axis; a window cut to its edge runs a duotone photo; big digits stamp one per eighth, the unit in red
- id: pita merah menghantam sumbu -18 derajat; jendela di tepinya memutar foto dua nada; angka besar dicetak satu per satu, satuan merah

## problem

- en: a document sits on an ink ground, a red marker bar crosses the exact sentence, a huge red question block repeats it
- id: dokumen di atas latar tinta, batang penanda merah melintasi kalimatnya, blok merah besar mengulangnya

## fact

- en: a tilted document map pushes in; a red circle is drawn round the place and becomes an iris; a red lower third states the fact
- id: peta dokumen miring mendekat; lingkaran merah digambar di tempatnya lalu jadi iris; pita merah bawah menyebut faktanya

## step

- en: a slanted window of photo beside type stacked top to bottom, letters slammed one per sixteenth; a date on a band and a counter climbing
- id: jendela miring berisi foto di samping huruf bertumpuk tegak, dihantam satu per enam belasan; tanggal di pita, penghitung naik

## compare

- en: two photos alternate faster (a machine cut, ground flipping ink and paper) until a held red block states what the collision means
- id: dua foto bergantian makin cepat (potongan mesin, latar berganti tinta dan kertas) sampai blok merah menyatakan maknanya

## number

- en: numbers as beams, 360 px and up, slammed from the left with the unit on a red block; the key number restamped on red
- id: angka sebagai balok, 360 px ke atas, dihantam dari kiri dengan satuan di blok merah; angka kuncinya dicetak ulang di merah

## proof

- en: flash cut to a frozen photo, a red ellipse drawn on the object with a leader to a block with the figure; then a jump-in crop
- id: potong kilat ke foto beku, elips merah digambar di objeknya dengan garis ke blok berisi angka; lalu potong masuk lebih dekat

## offer

- en: a result composition: huge numbers left, a tall slanted window with the finished subject, a red band with the offer along the axis
- id: komposisi hasil: angka raksasa di kiri, jendela miring tinggi berisi hasil jadi, pita merah berisi tawaran di sumbu

## cta

- en: ink silence with one red dot, then the heaviest hit; contact on a tilted paper slip; everything locks and holds 2 s
- id: hening di atas tinta dengan satu titik merah, lalu hantaman terberat; kontak di secarik kertas miring; semua terkunci diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the finished subject in a tall slanted window, the camera tilting up it, the key number on red; locked and held 2 s
- id: hasil jadi di jendela miring tinggi, kamera naik perlahan, angka kunci di merah; terkunci dan ditahan 2 detik

    <script>
      window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
      const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
      const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
      // PRNG berbiji (mulberry32): sama di pratinjau dan render.
      let seed = 41;
      function rnd() {
        seed = (seed + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0;
        let t = Math.imul(seed ^ (seed >>> 15), 1 | seed);
        t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
        return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
      }
      /* ---------- Cetak dua nada: foto digambar abu-abu, lalu tinta -> kertas ---------- */
      const cs = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
      const hex = (v) => [1, 3, 5].map((i) => parseInt(v.trim().slice(i, i + 2), 16));
      let ink = hex(cs.getPropertyValue("--teks"));
      let paper = hex(cs.getPropertyValue("--latar"));
      const lum = (c) => c[0] * 0.2 + c[1] * 0.7 + c[2] * 0.1;
      if (lum(ink) > lum(paper)) [ink, paper] = [paper, ink];
      const gray = (v) => `rgb(${v},${v},${v})`;
      function sheet(w, h, draw, grade, mime = "image/jpeg") {
        const c = document.createElement("canvas");
        c.width = w;
        c.height = h;
        const g = c.getContext("2d");
        draw(g, w, h);
        if (grade) {
          const im = g.getImageData(0, 0, w, h);
          const d = im.data;
          for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) {
            let x = d[i] / 255;
            x += 0.32 * (x - 0.5) * (1 - Math.abs(2 * x - 1)) * 2 + (rnd() - 0.5) * 0.06; // kurva S + butir
            x = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, x));
            for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) d[i + k] = ink[k] + (paper[k] - ink[k]) * x;
          }
          g.putImageData(im, 0, 0);
        }
        return c["toDataURL"](mime, 0.86);
      }
      function put(data, parent) {
        const img = new Image();
        Object.assign(img, { src: data });
        parent.prepend(img);
      }
      function person(g, x, y, s, v, lean, hat) {
        g.fillStyle = gray(v);
        g.beginPath();
        g.arc(x, y - s * 3.5, s * 0.55, 0, 6.3);
        if (hat) g.lineTo(x, y - s * 4.8);
        g.fill();
        g.save();
        g.translate(x, y);
        g.rotate(lean);
        g.fillRect(-s * 0.7, -s * 3, s * 1.4, s * 3);
